intro.author: Traditionally John son of Zebedee, identified with 'the disciple whom Jesus loved' (21:20-24). The Gospel does not name him, and scholars discuss how the beloved disciple relates to the final writer.
intro.written: Most scholars date it about AD 90–100; early tradition places it in Ephesus
intro.audience: Believers and seekers across the Roman world, both Jewish and Gentile
intro.setting: John's Gospel is quite different from the other three. It records long conversations and speeches, much of Jesus' work in Judea, and several festival visits to Jerusalem, including three Passovers, which is why Jesus' ministry is often reckoned at about three years.
intro.purpose: 'That ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name' (20:31).
intro.bigIdea: The eternal Word became flesh, so that whoever believes in him has life.
